title: Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability
problemSolved: King’s does not yet have a sustained multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for moving emerging student-experience needs from discovery and prototype into secure, supported institutional operation.
whatChanges: King’s establishes a four-post funded digital product core to deliver King’s Edge and the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release while testing the capability model itself. The four funded Year One posts are explicit: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Mark Peace is the Product Owner. Business-analysis capacity and DevOps/platform support are expected as small protected shared allocations rather than additional funded core posts. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer, while specialist security, privacy, accessibility and architecture assurance are drawn from existing institutional functions when required. Solution architecture should be covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer role if credible; otherwise a small additional shared allocation is required. A 1.0 FTE sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer is retained as an optional augmentation only, not as a replacement for the middleweight engineer and not included in the current baseline. The current Year One staffing envelope is £201,000 for approximately November 2026 to June 2027, pending Digital and IT grading, start dates and confirmation of whether QA starts later. Agentic software-development tooling remains an optional productivity investment to be validated separately and is not included in the Year One baseline. Evidence from delivery and discovery then determines the enduring team shape and any future expansion.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that the 4.0 FTE funded product pod remains the Year One core. Broad digital-estate mapping and student-journey discovery require additional named and protected service-design and business-analysis capacity, with reliable user-research support. The planning assumption is to secure this through existing or seconded institutional capability where possible, without tying it to a particular organisational home or automatically enlarging the permanent pod. Specialist technical and assurance inputs remain time-bound and should be explicitly protected when needed.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Revised and clarified the Year One four-person product-core hypothesis. The funded posts are 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE UX/UI design capacity and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. QA may start later once code production is established. Digital and IT will confirm whether the senior engineering post can also fulfil solution architecture or whether architecture must be supplied separately.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed the mobilisation route: Education secures the investment through the strategic funding process and Digital and IT creates and recruits the technical roles through its workforce processes. The existing KAI team will not be transferred wholesale into the Hub capability, although reusable technical assets should be assessed deliberately, including Azure AI Foundry components.

decisionLog.forum: Digital Experience Hub alignment conversation with Digital and IT
decisionLog.outcome: Agentic software development should be incorporated into the Year One delivery model as an accelerator used by an experienced engineering team. Any incremental tooling cost must be validated by Digital and IT and is not part of the baseline Year One funding ask until that validation is complete.

Simplified the Year One capability model for Digital and IT validation. Mark Peace is the Product Owner. The funded design post is defined as a Product & Service Designer combining UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer; specialist security, privacy, accessibility and architecture assurance remain institutional specialist inputs. Remove the previous separate delivery/agile, service-design, user-research and pooled-assurance FTE assumptions. Retain only small protected shared Business Analyst and DevOps/platform allocations, with conditional solution-architecture support if the senior engineer cannot carry it. A 1.0 FTE sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer may be added as optional augmentation but must not replace the middleweight engineer in the baseline.
